data.gender_notes: Alihat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the name 'Ali', meaning 'high-ranking', 'elevated', or 'sublime'. In Islamic history, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib was the fourth caliph and a cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad. The name Alihat carries the meaning “Exalted, Noble” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Alihat usually hope their child will grow to embody exalted, noble and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alihat total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.context: Ali, the fourth Rightly-Guided Caliph of Islam, assumed the title 'Alihat' during the Battle of Siffin (657 CE) to distinguish himself from Mu'awiya, the Umayyad claimant to the caliphate.
